question: A 10-month-old male infant on a diet of boiled cow's milk and no fruit/vegetables presents with severe irritability, refusal to move his legs, and subperiosteal haematoma on X-ray (Pelkan's spur and Trummerfeld zone). His gums appear normal. Which statement best explains the gum finding?

answers.text: The absence of gum bleeding makes scurvy unlikely — gum bleeding is a mandatory feature of scurvy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Gum bleeding is NOT a mandatory feature in infants. Gum bleeding in scurvy requires erupted teeth; an infant with no teeth cannot show gingival bleeding. Scurvy is still the correct diagnosis.

answers.text: Infants with scurvy cannot have gum bleeding because they have no erupted teeth; the diagnosis remains scurvy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. This is the key clinical trap: classic gum bleeding (spongy, bleeding gums) only occurs around erupted teeth. An infant without teeth will NOT have gingival bleeding, yet can have severe scurvy. The diagnosis rests on the subperiosteal haematoma, irritability, and dietary history.

answers.text: Normal gums indicate the disease has not progressed beyond Stage 1 scurvy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Scurvy is not staged by gum bleeding. The absence of gum bleeding in a toothless infant is expected and does not indicate mild disease — this infant has subperiosteal haematoma, which is a severe feature.

answers.text: The normal gums suggest a concurrent Vitamin K deficiency rather than scurvy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Vitamin K deficiency causes coagulopathy (prolonged PT/aPTT), not subperiosteal haematoma and pseudoparalysis. The X-ray finding of Pelkan's spur and Trummerfeld zone is pathognomonic of scurvy.

overallFeedback.feedback: The clinical pearl: infants with scurvy have no teeth, so gum bleeding is absent. The diagnosis of scurvy is made on subperiosteal haematoma, pseudoparalysis, and dietary history — not on gum bleeding.
Correct. Gum bleeding in scurvy requires teeth — a toothless infant will not show this sign, but can still have severe scurvy.
